title: Add Helm values for hardware tuning profile pack + override controls
author: Diego Santos
release_notes: Helm charts now support configuring the hardware tuning profile pack (enable/disable, pack version/source) and explicit override behavior for Dedicated/Private deployments. Defaults are safe (profiles disabled unless explicitly enabled; version pin required for external bundles).
body: Title: Add Helm values for hardware tuning profile pack + override controls Context: Runtime now supports loading a versioned hardware tuning profile pack (H100/B200/L40S) and selecting an effective profile based on GPU SKU + deployment overrides (see runtime PRs: redwood/pr-21991, redwood/pr-22027). Dedicated/Private installs need a supported way to (a) ship the profile pack bundle alongside the runtime, (b) pin the pack version, and (c) control override order without requiring ad-hoc ConfigMap edits that drift from supported configs. What this PR does: Wires profile pack configuration into the redwood-runtime chart values and templates, adds docs for operators, and keeps backward compatibility with existing runtimeConfig.* values. Key behavior is intentionally conservative: profiles remain OFF by default and the chart will not change runtime behavior unless the operator explicitly enables the profile pack. Summary of changes (operator-facing): 1) New values under runtime.hardwareProfiles.* (Dedicated/Private): - runtime.hardwareProfiles.enabled (default: false) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.pack.version (required when enabled for external sources; optional for builtin) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.pack.source: "builtin" | "configMap" | "inline" (default: "builtin") - runtime.hardwareProfiles.pack.configMapName (used when source=configMap) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.pack.inlineJson (used when source=inline; intended for testing only) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.override.allowEnvOverrides (default: true) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.override.allowHelmValueOverrides (default: true) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.override.lockProfileName (default: ""; when set, pins a specific profile name and disables auto-detect) - runtime.hardwareProfiles.override.precedence (default: "env,helm,fleet,autodetect") 2) Chart templates mount the pack and plumb settings to runtime via env vars/args, consistent with the runtime loader’s precedence rules: Effective config is determined in this order by default: (1) explicit env overrides (intended for oncall / emergency mitigation), then (2) Helm-provided overrides (values.yaml / per-install), then (3) fleet defaults (if present in private-control-plane integration), then (4) GPU SKU autodetect (H100/B200/L40S) with safe fallback to "generic". If the runtime cannot safely detect SKU or the pack/version is incompatible, it falls back to runtime defaults and emits a startup log warning (no crash-loop by default). 3) Adds documentation: - docs/README.md section: “Hardware tuning profile pack” - values.yaml examples for: Dedicated H100 pool, Private install w/ ConfigMap bundle, emergency disable via env var - explicit wording around “expected behavior” vs guarantees (aligns with SRE feedback) Notes on safe defaults / compatibility: - enabled=false by default to avoid unexpected perf/latency changes on upgrade. - When enabled and source=configMap, version pin is required to avoid silent drift. - If lockProfileName is set, chart renders a validation warning in NOTES.txt if enabled but no profile is found at startup (runtime-level). - B200 remains experimental; this chart does not auto-enable B200-specific profile—operators must opt-in by enabling profiles and allowing autodetect/lockProfileName as appropriate (runtime gating remains enforced by runtime feature flag and compatibility checks). Implementation details: - Adds templates/hardware-profiles-configmap.yaml when runtime.hardwareProfiles.pack.source=inline (test/dev only) - Adds volume+mount for configMap source and sets RUNTIME_PROFILE_PACK_PATH for runtime - Adds env wiring for: RUNTIME_HARDWARE_PROFILES_ENABLED, RUNTIME_PROFILE_PACK_VERSION, RUNTIME_PROFILE_OVERRIDE_PRECEDENCE, RUNTIME_PROFILE_LOCK_NAME, RUNTIME_PROFILE_ALLOW_ENV_OVERRIDES - Updates templates/NOTES.txt to include operator guidance + quick verification commands (kubectl exec + runtime debug endpoint) Testing: - helm lint and chart unit tests updated - Verified rendered manifests for: (a) Dedicated with no profiles (no changes vs prior render), (b) Private with configMap bundle, (c) inline bundle smoke for CI - Manual sanity: runtime starts when bundle missing (enabled=false), and fails “softly” (warn + fallback) when enabled but bundle path invalid (relies on runtime behavior; no crash loop introduced by chart). Rollout: - This is required for the staged profile pack rollout in Dedicated/Private (ENG-4830). Hosted will consume pack internally and does not use this chart. Follow-ups: - Consider adding a chart-level schema check once runtime schema keys are finalized (will land after ENG-4822 stabilizes). - Add a helper to generate ConfigMap from a profile pack tarball for Private operators (separate tooling task).
changed_areas: charts/redwood-runtime/README.md (hardware profiles section, override order, examples)
.github/workflows/chart-ci.yml (adds a render case with profiles enabled via inline bundle)
commits: Add runtime.hardwareProfiles values and comments to values.yaml
Template: mount profile pack bundle and wire env vars/args
Docs: describe override order, safe defaults, and Private/Dedicated examples
Tests: update golden renders + add profile-enabled render case
review_conversation: Keiko Yamamoto: Can we make sure enabling profiles doesn’t change autoscaling by default? Some pools have tight memory headroom. Diego Santos: Yes—this PR only wires the pack + override controls. Autoscaling knobs remain unchanged. Also left enabled=false default to avoid surprises.

Ethan Park: Precedence string feels fragile; can we constrain to known tokens? Diego Santos: Added docs with allowed tokens and a NOTES.txt warning; runtime validates and falls back to default precedence if malformed (as per loader implementation).

Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please add an explicit emergency disable path that doesn’t require Helm upgrade during incident. Diego Santos: Added allowEnvOverrides=true default and documented setting RUNTIME_HARDWARE_PROFILES_ENABLED=0 as the fastest mitigation; also added NOTES.txt snippet.

Nina Petrova: ConfigMap name should be namespaced/predictable to avoid collisions in multi-release namespaces. Diego Santos: Kept it operator-provided (configMapName), but for inline source the generated ConfigMap uses {{ include "redwood-runtime.fullname" }}-hardware-profiles to remain per-release unique.

Connor O'Brien: Any upgrade notes? If someone upgrades chart but had previously hacked in a mount, will it break? Diego Santos: Added a doc note: the new values are optional; existing custom mounts still work, but we recommend moving to supported keys. No template behavior changes unless enabled=true.
notes_for_oncall: If a regression is suspected after enabling profiles in a Dedicated/Private pool, set env var RUNTIME_HARDWARE_PROFILES_ENABLED=0 (or set runtime.hardwareProfiles.enabled=false and redeploy). Verify selected profile via runtime metrics (profile_selected, profile_override_source) and/or debug endpoint as documented in NOTES.txt.
